svg.text: Two Different Times: Module Load vs. Request Handling
PHASE 1 — Module load time (happens ONCE, at process startup)
Node loads clientFactory.ts for the first time — triggered by the very first "import" of it, anywhere in the app.
This line runs immediately, top to bottom, as part of loading the file — NOT when discoverProtocol() is called.
Node then CACHES the finished module. Every future "import ... from clientFactory" reuses this same cached copy —
the file's top-level code never runs a second time, no matter how many files import from it.
PHASE 2 — Request time (happens EVERY TIME a device is registered)
A POST /devices request arrives. MonitoringService.registerDevice() runs, and calls:
discoverProtocol is a plain function living in clientFactory.ts. It reads "restClient" — a variable declared
ABOVE it, in the SAME file. This is ordinary JavaScript closure/scope, not dependency injection: any function
can see any variable declared earlier in its own module, the same way it can see an imported name.
restClient already exists by this point — it was built once, back in Phase 1, long before this request arrived.
This whole phase can run thousands of times. Phase 1 never runs again.
Verified live: the constructor log line printed exactly once, before any request-time code ran — see demo output above.
